answer: Treat the agent economy as a trust graph where every agent is a vertex and every verified transaction is an edge. A new vertex starts with no inbound edges and earns nothing until established peers attest its real work, so a Sybil swarm arriving at dawn with thousands of identities holds zero trust. Each fake must separately earn attestations through sustained useful work, so cost scales with the number of fakes. Like ships queuing at a wharf, newcomers wait for verification, and graph analysis spots clusters that only attest each other, with no links to the honest core, and quarantines them.
